title: Builder (creational)
points: Builds an object with many (often optional) parameters step by step.
A static nested Builder class has one method per parameter, each returning the builder, plus a final build(). A static builder() on the outer class is the entry point.
trade: Fixes the telescoping constructor problem. The result can be immutable and build() is one place to validate. Fluent chain is fine under Law of Demeter. Overkill for 2-3 required params. Lombok @Builder generates it.
test: A class has 8 fields, 5 of them optional. Why is a builder better than overloaded constructors, and where should validation go?
answer: Named, readable steps instead of guessing which argument is which, and no explosion of constructors. Validate once in build().

questions.question: A class has 8 fields, 5 optional, and callers can't tell which constructor argument is which. What helps most?
questions.explanation: Builder: named steps, defaults for optional fields, and validation once in build().
